Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$ with $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$
and $m\ge n$.

1. Successive Householder reflectors or Givens transformations can zero the
   subdiagonal entries column by column and produce a full QR factorisation
   $A=QR$ and hence a reduced QR factorisation $A=\widehat Q\widehat R$.
2. In dense real arithmetic, Householder QR uses
   $$2mn^2-\frac{2}{3}n^3+O(mn)$$
   scalar operations, while dense Givens QR uses
   $$3mn^2-n^3+O(mn)$$
   scalar operations.

Assume AC, and let $d,n,p$ be positive integers. Let $U\in\mathbb R^d$,
$q\in\mathbb R^n$, and $r\in\mathbb R^p$ be mutually independent Gaussian vectors with
$$U\sim N_d(m,P),\qquad q\sim N_n(0,Q),\qquad r\sim N_p(0,R),$$
where $P,Q,R$ are symmetric positive semidefinite. Let
$F\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ and $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$, and set
$$X=FU+q,\qquad Y=HX+r,\qquad P^-:=FPF^T+Q,\qquad S:=HP^-H^T+R.$$
If $S$ is positive definite, put $K:=P^-H^TS^{-1}$. Then $(X,Y)$ is jointly
Gaussian with mean $(Fm,HFm)$ and covariance
$$\begin{pmatrix}P^-&P^-H^T\\HP^-&S\end{pmatrix},$$
and for every $y\in\mathbb R^p$ an everywhere-defined conditional law is
$$\mathcal L(X\mid Y=y)=N_n\!\left(Fm+K(y-HFm),\,P^--KSK^T\right).$$
The conditional covariance is positive semidefinite even if $P$, $Q$, or
$R$ is singular. It also equals the Joseph expression
$$(I-KH)P^-(I-KH)^T+KRK^T.$$
No inverse of a state, process-noise, or measurement-noise covariance is
used.

derivations.claim: Multiplying the prearray by its transpose and using $P^-=L^-(L^-)^T$ gives $$ZZ^T=\begin{bmatrix} L_R^{\mathrm{pad}}(L_R^{\mathrm{pad}})^T+HL^-(L^-)^TH^T&HL^-(L^-)^T\\ L^-(L^-)^TH^T&L^-(L^-)^T \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix}S&HP^-\\P^-H^T&P^- \end{bmatrix}.$$ The zero padding leaves $L_RL_R^T$ unchanged.

Since $Z^T=UR$ and $U^TU=I$, $LL^T=R^TR=ZZ^T$. Block multiplication therefore yields $L_{11}L_{11}^T=S$, $L_{21}L_{11}^T=P^-H^T$, and $L_{21}L_{21}^T+L_{22}L_{22}^T=P^-$. Exact diagonal sign changes multiply rows of $R$ by an orthogonal diagonal matrix and preserve $R^TR$, so these identities survive the positive-diagonal normalization.

Because $S\succ0$ and $S=L_{11}L_{11}^T$, the square matrix $L_{11}$ is invertible. From the cross-block identity, $L_{21}=P^-H^T L_{11}^{-T}$; hence $$L_{21}L_{21}^T=P^-H^TL_{11}^{-T}L_{11}^{-1}HP^- =P^-H^TS^{-1}HP^-.$$ Subtracting this equality from the lower-right identity in step 2.1 gives the stated posterior covariance. Since it is also $L_{22}L_{22}^T$, it is positive semidefinite even when $L_{22}$ is singular.

The solve $L_{11}z=v$ gives $$L_{21}z=L_{21}L_{11}^{-1}v =P^-H^TL_{11}^{-T}L_{11}^{-1}v =P^-H^TS^{-1}v.$$ By [F2], these mean and covariance are the one-step Gaussian conditional update. The matrix calculations themselves are deterministic and use no choice beyond [A1].

Let $n\ge 1$ and let $x=(x_j),y=(y_j)\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$, with the dot product
$x\cdot y=\sum_{j<n}x_jy_j$ computed from left to right in an arithmetic model
with unit roundoff $u$ satisfying $nu<1$
([[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]]), where every
product $x_jy_j$, every rounded product
$p_j:=\operatorname{fl}(x_jy_j)$, and every intermediate sum lies in the normal
range. Let $s_1:=p_0$ and, for $1\le k<n$, let
$s_{k+1}:=\operatorname{fl}(s_k+p_k)$. Then:

1. **Componentwise form.** There are reals $\delta_0,\dots,\delta_{n-1}$ with
   $|\delta_j|\le\gamma_n:=nu/(1-nu)$ such that
   $$s_n=\sum_{j<n}x_jy_j(1+\delta_j).$$
2. **Normwise form.**
   $$|s_n-x\cdot y|\;\le\;\gamma_n\sum_{j<n}|x_jy_j|\;\le\;\gamma_n\,\lVert x\rVert_1\lVert y\rVert_1,$$
   where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_1$ is the published $1$-norm
   ([[def-p-norms-on-rn]], [[lem-p-norms-are-norms-and-induce-the-published-metrics]])
   and $|\cdot|$ the absolute value ([[def-abs-value]]).

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $m\ge n\ge1$, undergo successful QR steps of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], with $mu<1$. Use $\kappa_m$ from [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]] and set $\beta_Q=(1+\kappa_m)^n-1$. The exact orthogonal product represented by the stored reflectors has reduced first $n$ columns $\widehat Q$, and the computed triangular block is $\widehat R$. Then
$$A+\Delta A=\widehat Q\widehat R,\qquad \|\Delta A\|_F\le\beta_Q\|A\|_F.$$
If applying the stored reflectors in the same order to a separate vector $b$, by their rounded rank-one updates without column overwrites, succeeds at every update, the resulting full vector $\widehat c$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat c-Q_{\rm full}^Tb\|_2\le\beta_Q\|b\|_2.$$
The bounds are $O(u)$ for fixed dimensions. An explicitly rounded dense product for $Q_{\rm full}$ is not asserted exactly orthogonal.

Let $G,E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and set $\widehat G=G+E$. Then
$$\|\widehat G\widehat G^T-GG^T\|_F \le 2\|G\|_F\|E\|_F+\|E\|_F^2.$$
The estimate is valid for all ranks, including $G=0$ and rank-deficient
factors.

Let $q\ge n\ge1$, $u>0$, and let $\kappa_q$ be the local scaled-Householder
coefficient of [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]]
at active row dimension $q$. Set

Disjoint product blocks add by the Frobenius norm definition, and separately bounded input-factor errors add by the triangle inequality.

Apply [F2] to $\widehat G^T$, which has $q\ge n$ rows and $n$ columns. Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_k$ for
$0\le k\le T$, and positive observation dimensions $p_k$ for
$1\le k\le T$. Inputs are real finite matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times
d_{k-1}}$, $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, observation vectors
$y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$, and an initial mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$.
For each covariance supply a rectangular real factor
$$L_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times r_0},\qquad L_{Q,k}\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times r_{Q,k}},\qquad L_{R,k}\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times r_{R,k}},$$
where each column count is any finite nonnegative integer. The represented
covariances are $P_0=L_0L_0^T$, $Q_k=L_{Q,k}L_{Q,k}^T$, and
$R_k=L_{R,k}L_{R,k}^T$. Thus zero columns and rank-deficient factors are
allowed. The admissible statistical inputs are those of
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] for which
the canonical innovation $S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k$ is positive definite at each
step. The [[def-axiom-of-choice]] assumption is inherited only for the
interpretation as a posterior; the finite matrix procedure itself uses no
probability-space choice.

Choose a unit roundoff $u$ in the no-underflow operationwise model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Every matrix or vector product below is evaluated as left-to-right dot
products. A nonzero nonnormal intermediate, nonfinite result, zero innovation
diagonal, or failed factorization returns a status and the first failing step;
it is not coerced into a covariance
estimate. Each arithmetic and factorization failure has a declared return;
there is no iterative convergence loop or unbounded refinement search.

The QR operation used below is the following unpivoted reduced procedure on
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n\ge1$. Initialize a working array
$R^{(0)}=A$ and an empty ordered reflector list. For $j=1,\ldots,n$, take
$x=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j}$ and $B=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j+1:n}$, call
[[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] on $(x,B)$,
and, on success, replace the active block by its returned $C_+$. If the call
fails, return its first status and step. Store the exact orthogonal reflector
represented by the returned record, or the identity for its identity branch.
After $n$ successful steps, return the computed upper-triangular block
$R=R^{(n)}_{1:n,1:n}$ and the ordered reflector list representing the exact
product $Q_{\rm full}$ whose first $n$ columns are the reduced $Q$ factor.
Do not materialize a rounded dense $Q$. The conventions are those of
[[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]].

Initialize $m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $L_{0|0}=L_0$. At step $k$, perform the
following operations in order.

1. Compute the rounded mean prediction $\widehat m_{k|k-1}
=\operatorname{fl}(F_k\widehat m_{k-1|k-1})$. Form the rounded factor product
$\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}(F_kL_{k-1|k-1})$. Concatenate
$\widehat G_k=[\widehat X_k\;L_{Q,k}]$ and append zero columns until its
column count is $q_k=\max(d_k,r_{k-1|k-1}+r_{Q,k})$. Apply the above
reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat G_k^T\in\mathbb R^{q_k\times d_k}$. On success let $R_k^{p}$ be
its reduced upper factor and set $L_{k|k-1}= (R_k^{p})^T$. No diagonal
positivity or full-rank condition is imposed on this prediction factor.

2. Compute $\widehat v_k=\operatorname{fl}
(y_k-\operatorname{fl}(H_k\widehat m_{k|k-1}))$. Pad $L_{R,k}$ with zero
columns to $\bar r_k=\max(p_k,r_{R,k})$ columns. Compute
$\widehat Y_k=\operatorname{fl}(H_kL_{k|k-1})$ and form the block prearray
$$\widehat Z_k= \begin{bmatrix} L_{R,k}^{\mathrm{pad}} & \widehat Y_k\\ 0 & L_{k|k-1} \end{bmatrix}.$$
Apply the above reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat Z_k^T\in\mathbb R^{(\bar r_k+d_k)\times(p_k+d_k)}$. Its row
count is at least its column count. On success transpose its reduced upper
factor and partition the resulting lower factor as
$$\widehat L_k=\begin{bmatrix}\widehat L_{11,k}&0\\ \widehat L_{21,k}&\widehat L_{22,k}\end{bmatrix},$$
with block sizes $p_k$ and $d_k$. If any diagonal entry of $\widehat
L_{11,k}$ is zero, return `innovation-factorization-failure`. Otherwise,
multiply each row of the QR upper factor corresponding to that block by the
sign of its diagonal entry, an exact sign change, so that
$\widehat L_{11,k}$ has positive diagonal. This changes neither
$\widehat L_k\widehat L_k^T$ nor its lower block structure. No invertibility
or positive diagonal is required of $\widehat L_{22,k}$.

3. Solve $\widehat L_{11,k}\widehat z_k=\widehat v_k$ by forward
substitution in the order of
[[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]]. Set
$$\widehat m_{k|k}=\operatorname{fl} (\widehat m_{k|k-1}+\widehat L_{21,k}\widehat z_k),\qquad L_{k|k}=\widehat L_{22,k}.$$
Do not form a covariance downdate or an explicit matrix inverse. The
factor-defined covariance $L_{k|k}L_{k|k}^T$ is positive semidefinite as an
exact product of the returned entries; no claim is made that a separately
rounded materialization of that product remains positive semidefinite.

4. If any arithmetic operation or QR call returns a failure status, return the
first such failure and its step; if the leading innovation block has a zero
diagonal, return innovation-factorization-failure. Otherwise the finite loop
returns the predicted and updated mean/factor arrays with success. The success
status records arithmetic and factorization completion only.

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the output is $(m_0,L_0)$ with no update
status. In exact arithmetic, the result implements the covariance and mean map of
[[alg-kalman-filter]]. The prediction factor identity is supplied by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-prediction-factor-identity]], and the measurement
block identity by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-measurement-block-factor-identity]]. Under the
inherited AC assumption
its statistical interpretation is the one in
[[thm-kalman-filter-is-exact-posterior]]. The nearby covariance supplied by
an unstructured QR backward error may introduce cross-correlations between
model blocks. Therefore no backward-stability claim within the original
independent-noise state-space model, and no uniform-in-time accuracy or
stability claim, is part of this procedure.

On every admitted finite input of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], the formation and application procedure terminates with its specified identity, reflector or first-failure return. Each specified separate-block application also terminates with its output or first failure. The zero-column branch returns the identity action and the copied block without evaluating a reflector denominator. In a successful nonzero-column branch the stored vector is nonzero, so its associated exact real reflector is orthogonal and also acts unitarily on complex blocks. This statement asserts neither unconditional arithmetic success nor a backward-error bound for a successful call.

Let $F$ be a field, let $n\ge 1$, and let $b\in F^n$.

If $L=(\ell_{ij})\in M_n(F)$ is lower triangular with every diagonal entry
$\ell_{ii}\ne 0$, the **forward substitution solve** of $Lx=b$ is the recursive
construction

$$x_i:=\frac{1}{\ell_{ii}}\left(b_i-\sum_{j<i}\ell_{ij}x_j\right)\qquad(0\le i<n).$$If $U=(u_{ij})\in M_n(F)$ is upper triangular with every diagonal entry $u_{ii}\ne 0$, the **backward substitution solve** of $Ux=b$ is the recursive construction$$x_i:=\frac{1}{u_{ii}}\left(b_i-\sum_{j>i}u_{ij}x_j\right)\qquad(n-1\ge i\ge 0).$$

The triangular vocabulary is from
[[def-triangular-and-diagonal-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]. The matrix
product convention from [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] is the one
used when later items rewrite these recursions as matrix equations.

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$,
and positive observation dimensions $p_1,\ldots,p_T$. The input is a
linear-Gaussian model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with
matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$ and
$H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, initial mean $m_0$, and symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$. Its state and observation
equations are
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k,$$
where $q_k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $r_k\sim N(0,R_k)$ are centered and mutually
independent across all times and of $X_0$.

The admissible data are vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$ for which every
innovation covariance encountered below is positive definite. Positive
definite means $u^TS_ku>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. The
algorithm returns predicted and updated means and covariances and the
innovation and gain at each time. Initialize
$$m_{0|0}=m_0,\qquad P_{0|0}=P_0.$$
For $k=1,\ldots,T$, perform:

1. Predict:
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k.$$
2. Form the innovation and its covariance:
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
3. Factor $S_k=L_kL_k^T$ with lower-triangular $L_k$ having positive
diagonal, using
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Solve $L_kU_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}$ and $L_k^TK_k^T=U_k$ by triangular solves. This
defines $K_k^T=S_k^{-1}H_kP_{k|k-1}$, hence
$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, without explicitly forming $S_k^{-1}$.
4. Update:
$$m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the returned pair is $(m_0,P_0)$. No
inverse of $P_0$, $Q_k$, or $R_k$ is used. This item defines the procedure
and makes no complexity, rounding-error, or numerical-stability claim.

Let $P^-=L^- (L^-)^T$ and $R=L_RL_R^T$, with real factors of arbitrary
rank. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and suppose
$$S=H P^-H^T+R\succ0.$$
Pad $L_R$ with zero columns so it has at least $p$ columns and form
$$Z=\begin{bmatrix}L_R^{\mathrm{pad}}&HL^-\\0&L^-\end{bmatrix}.$$
Take an exact reduced QR factorization $Z^T=UR$ with $U^TU=I$, set
$L=R^T$, and partition
$$L=\begin{bmatrix}L_{11}&0\\L_{21}&L_{22}\end{bmatrix}$$
at the observation and state dimensions. If needed, multiply each of the
first $p$ rows of $R$ by the sign of its diagonal entry, so that $L_{11}$ has
positive diagonal. Then
$$L_{11}L_{11}^T=S,\qquad L_{21}L_{11}^T=P^-H^T,$$
and
$$L_{22}L_{22}^T=P^- -P^-H^TS^{-1}HP^-.$$
For innovation $v=y-Hm^-$, the exact solve $L_{11}z=v$ gives
$m^-+L_{21}z=m^-+P^-H^TS^{-1}v$. Thus the factor update has exactly the
canonical one-step mean and covariance; $L_{22}$ may be singular.

Let $G\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, with $q\ge n$, be an exact prediction or
measurement prearray. Let $\widehat G$ be its computed version and assume
$$\|\widehat G-G\|_F\le e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}},$$
where $e_{\mathrm{form}},e_{\mathrm{in}}\ge0$, $e_{\mathrm{form}}$ bounds
rounded products used to form the array, and $e_{\mathrm{in}}$ bounds
separately specified input-factor uncertainty. If
the successful scaled-Householder QR of $\widehat G^T\in\mathbb R^{q\times
n}$ has reduced upper factor $R$ and $L=R^T$, set
$$\kappa_q=\kappa_q(u),\qquad \beta_{q,n}=(1+\kappa_q)^n-1,\qquad \epsilon=e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}}+ \beta_{q,n}\|\widehat G\|_F,$$
where $\kappa_q$ is the explicit local coefficient in
[[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]]. Then
$$\|LL^T-GG^T\|_F\le2\|G\|_F\epsilon+\epsilon^2.$$
If $200qnu<1$, the rational envelope lemma
[[lem-square-root-kalman-householder-error-rational-envelope]] gives
$\beta_{q,n}\le\eta_{q,n}:=200qnu/(1-200qnu)$. In that regime the same
conclusion holds with
$\epsilon=e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}}+\eta_{q,n}\|\widehat G\|_F$.
For one left-to-right rounded product $\widehat{UV}$ with inner dimension
$r$ and $ru<1$, a valid choice is
$e_{\mathrm{form}}=\gamma_r\|U\|_F\|V\|_F$; for several disjoint product
blocks, sum these bounds. This conclusion allows rank loss and does not imply
that the nearby joint covariance has the original independent-noise block
structure.

Let $S=S^T\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ satisfy
$x^TSx\ge\mu\|x\|_2^2$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^p$, with $\mu>0$.
Let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $D=D^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and
let symmetric $E_S$ and matrices $E_B,E_D$ satisfy
$$\|E_S\|_F\le e_S<\mu,\qquad \|E_B\|_F\le e_B,\qquad \|E_D\|_F\le e_D.$$
Put $\widehat S=S+E_S$, $\widehat B=B+E_B$,
$\widehat D=D+E_D$, $\Phi=D-BS^{-1}B^T$, and
$\widehat\Phi=\widehat D-\widehat B\widehat S^{-1}\widehat B^T$.
If $b\ge\|B\|_2$, define $\beta=(\mu-e_S)^{-1}$. Then
$\widehat S\succeq(\mu-e_S)I\succ0$ and
$$\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2\le\beta,\qquad \|\widehat S^{-1}-S^{-1}\|_2\le\mu^{-1}\beta e_S,$$
$$\|\widehat B\widehat S^{-1}-BS^{-1}\|_2 \le e_B\beta+b\mu^{-1}\beta e_S,$$
and
$$\|\widehat\Phi-\Phi\|_2 \le e_D+2b e_B\beta+b^2\mu^{-1}\beta e_S+e_B^2\beta.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $p\ge1$ and $T\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be nonsingular, define
$$
\sigma_{\min}(T):=\min_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Tx\|_2,
$$
and let $z_*=T^{-1}y$. For any computed vector $\widehat z$ with residual
$r=T\widehat z-y$,
$$
\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\frac{\|r\|_2}{\sigma_{\min}(T)}.
$$
If $S=TT^T$ also satisfies $x^TSx\ge\nu\|x\|_2^2$ for all $x$, with
$\nu>0$, then $\sigma_{\min}(T)\ge\sqrt\nu$ and therefore
$$
\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\frac{\|r\|_2}{\sqrt\nu}.
$$

derivations.claim: Put $\delta_{k-1}^P=\|\widehat P_{k-1|k-1}-P_{k-1|k-1}\|_2$ and $\delta_{k-1}^m=\|\widehat m_{k-1|k-1}-m_{k-1|k-1}\|_2$. By [F1] and the prediction defect, $$\|\widehat P_k^--P_k^-\|_2 \le f_k^2\delta_{k-1}^P+e_k^P,\qquad \|\widehat m_k^--m_k^-\|_2 \le f_k\delta_{k-1}^m+e_k^m.$$
